[LINT.2.2] Both operands must have one element type ([LINT.1.1]); an `Int`
and a `Float` have one ([LINT.1.2]). The compiler must refuse:

- operands of two element types, such as `some_date .. some_time` or an `Int`
  with a `String`, with `DS_VALIDATE_INTERVAL_MIXED_OPERANDS`;
- an operand of any type [LINT.1.1] does not list, with
  `DS_VALIDATE_UNORDERED_TYPE`: among them a `Bool`, a `Bytes` value, a whole
  `Json` value, a fact reference ([LEXP.7.19], [LEXP.7.20]), a value of an
  opaque type, whose `<` is sealed ([LOPQ.3.3]), and an interval.

An operand whose type is not known statically (a `Json` path read) is judged
by the ordinary type rules when the interval is used.
